Write and verify a recode manifest

Source: R/categorical_guard.R
wrrcdmnf.Rd

wrrcdmnf() saves a manifest from rcdmnf as a JSON file. vrfrcdmnf() reads such a file back and checks it against the data: that the mapping and the manifest body are unchanged since they were written, that the recode in the data still matches the recorded mapping, that the recoded counts are the recorded counts, and, for a signed manifest, that the signature verifies. Use the pair to hand a recode to a reviewer or to re-check it before a later analysis.

Usage

wrrcdmnf(man, path)

vrfrcdmnf(path, orig, recd)

Arguments

man

A manifest returned by rcdmnf.

path

Character string: the JSON file to write (wrrcdmnf()) or read (vrfrcdmnf()).

orig, recd

The vectors before and after the recode, to check the manifest against.

Value

wrrcdmnf() returns path invisibly.

vrfrcdmnf() returns a list with ok (logical), reasons (character; empty, character(0), when ok), signature_ok (logical, NA when the manifest is unsigned) and manifest (the parsed JSON as a list).

Details

vrfrcdmnf() collects every failure in reasons instead of stopping at the first:

  • the SHA-256 of the stored mapping differs from mapping_sha256;

  • the SHA-256 of the body (all fields except body_sha256, signature and public_key) differs from body_sha256, meaning the file was edited after it was written;

  • vrfrcd(original, recoded, mapping) fails;

  • the counts of recoded differ from counts_after.

The signature, when present, is checked with cpsvrf over the stored body_sha256. It therefore proves who wrote that hash; the body check above proves the body still matches it. Both are needed for ok = TRUE.

wrrcdmnf() errors when man is not a bricklayer_recode_manifest; it overwrites path.

Examples

x <- c("W", "B", "W")
y <- grdrcd(x, c(W = "White", B = "Black"))
m <- rcdmnf(x, y, c(W = "White", B = "Black"))
p <- wrrcdmnf(m, tempfile(fileext = ".json"))
vrfrcdmnf(p, x, y)$ok
#> [1] TRUE

# the data changed after the manifest was written
y2 <- y
y2[2] <- "White"
vrfrcdmnf(p, x, y2)$reasons
#> [1] "vrfrcd: ‘B’ was mapped to ‘White’ but the declared mapping says ‘Black’. THIS is how groups get swapped; fix the recode before any model runs."
#> [2] "recoded counts differ from the manifest"                                                                                                       

# only manifests can be written
try(wrrcdmnf(list(a = 1), tempfile()))
#> Error : wrrcdmnf: `man` must come from rcdmnf()
